name: Film & TV production assistant (category)
summary: Entry-level crew work on film, TV and commercial sets, sometimes reached through short crew-training programs. Job Bank files production assistants under NOC 53111.
whatYouDo: Production assistants (PAs) support crews on set and on location: running errands, helping move and set up equipment, managing people and traffic around the set, distributing paperwork and helping whichever department needs a hand. The work is on-site, usually by the day or by production, and long days are common.
appeal: A recognized way into Canada's screen industry that usually doesn't need a degree
Job Bank says the occupation usually requires a college diploma, an apprenticeship of under 2 years, or more than 6 months of on-the-job training
Free or low-cost crew-training programs have run in Toronto, Northern Ontario and B.C., some aimed at youth from under-represented groups
Toronto's earlier PA training program was recognized by the Directors Guild of Canada – Ontario toward its apprenticeship program, which cut the entry cost by 75% (City of Toronto, 2019)
watchOuts: Job Bank's 2025–2027 outlook is Very limited in Ontario and in the Montréal/Laval and Montérégie regions, Limited in Kitchener–Waterloo–Barrie and Moderate in Nova Scotia
Job Bank 'production assistant' wages ($16.00 low, $24.94 median, $36.49 high per hour) were last updated November 2023
Job Bank says these workers usually work more than 40 hours per week. Long, irregular days are typical
Work comes one production at a time, so income is irregular and depends on local filming activity
The training programs found (Toronto, Northern Ontario, B.C.) come from 2019–2023 reporting. No 2026 intake was confirmed

credentials: College diploma, apprenticeship under 2 years, or 6+ months on-the-job training usually expected (Job Bank)

training.notes: Some crew-training routes have been free (e.g. Northern Ontario crew training sessions, Reel Canada workshops); none confirmed running in 2026.

compensation.notes: Job Bank 'Production Assistant' Canada wages, last updated 29 Nov 2023: $16.00 low, $24.94 median, $36.49 high per hour. An undated Playback article reported PA day rates of $125–$150 at two Toronto commercial production companies (likely old). Current rates not verified.

reliability.notes: Project-based on-set work. Job Bank estimates about 2,200 workers in NOC 53111 in Ontario, with a Very limited outlook there for 2025–2027.

applicationSteps: Look for crew-training programs in your area (e.g. City of Toronto screen-industry pathways, Reel Canada's Reel Opportunities, regional film offices)
Search Job Bank and screen-industry job boards for production assistant postings
Build contacts with local crews, and ask about guild or union apprenticeship routes (e.g. Directors Guild of Canada – Ontario)
fitsIf: You like fast-paced, physical teamwork on location and can handle long days at short notice.
notFitIf: You need remote work, regular hours or steady weekly income.

sources.title: City of Toronto and partners launching program to train youth for work in local screen industry
sources.notes: Search summary (2019-era): five-week production assistant training for Black young adults aged 18–29 with POV and CEE Centre for Young Black Professionals; Directors Guild of Canada – Ontario counted the program toward its apprenticeship and cut entry cost 75%. Current status unknown. Page not opened.

sources.title: City of Toronto and partners announce expansion of screen industry workforce development training programs for diverse youth
sources.notes: Search summary (circa 2020–2021): expansion added an Indigenous cohort with Miziwe Biik and planned training for 200+ BIPOC participants with an $800,000 provincial grant. No 2025–2026 information found. Page not opened.

sources.title: Reel Opportunities workshops
sources.notes: Search summary: free one-hour classroom workshops with industry professionals for youth aged 14–30; program says it is expanding to in-person film and TV training in select cities (no cities, dates or pay details given). Page not opened.

sources.title: Training program feeds Northern Ontario's growing film/TV sector
sources.notes: Search summary: Cultural Industries Ontario North with Reel Canada ran free crew training in Sudbury, North Bay and Sault Ste. Marie covering production assistant, grip/electric and art department roles. Earlier year; not confirmed for 2026. Page not opened.

sources.title: Sparks, Partners' raise crew rates
sources.notes: Search summary: undated (likely old) report that two Toronto commercial production companies paid PAs $125–$150 per shoot day, with premiums for 14-hour days. Not current pay evidence. Page not opened.
